title: Starlight and laser light
caption: Yepun's laser guide star and the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Unit Telescope 4 of ESO's Very Large Telescope, named Yepun, shines a laser into the Milky Way, which stretches overhead as a bright band. The laser creates an artificial guide star.

That guide star belongs to the adaptive optics system on Yepun. By measuring how the atmosphere disturbs the artificial star's light, the system can correct for the same effects in astronomical images, making them clearer.

To the right stand the other three Unit Telescopes, named Antu, Kueyen and Melipal from left to right. Every one has a main mirror 8.2 meters across, placing them among the largest single-mirror telescopes anywhere. A single VLT telescope can detect objects four billion times fainter than anything visible to the unaided eye.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and the laser beam appear brighter than they would to someone on the platform.
